newsitem.title: PERU: India's Bharat in bid for Peru power deal.
newsitem.headline: India's Bharat in bid for Peru power deal.

text.p: Six foreign consortia have submitted proposals for the contract to supply equipment at the Peruvian government's planned San Gaban power station.
The Lima office of the United Nations Office for Projects' Services (UNOPS), which is overseeing the auctions of contracts, said the groups consisted of:
- Austria's Elin Energieversorgung GmbH and Italy's Voith Riva Hydro SpA.
- India's Bharat Heavy Electricals Ltd and Argentina's Industrias Metalurgicas Pescarmona SAIC y F.
- France's Cegelec SA and Brazil's Mecanica Pesada.
- Brazil's Tenenge, Germany's Siemens Aktiengesellschaft, and Norway's Kvaerner Energy aa.
- Spain's ABB Generacion SA and Switzerland's Hydro Vevey SA.
UNOPS officials said the winner of the contract would be announced around December 20. They could not say how much the contract might be worth.
The San Gaban power station, in the southeastern department of Puno, is expected to have a capacity of 110 megawatts and will initially serve Peru's southern region.

The United Nations was appointed to supervise the auction of construction and equipment contracts after a previous attempt to award them at the start of the year was overturned due to accusations of irregularities.
Three groups were chosen in August for the main contracts to construct the installations.
The Peruvian-Spanish consortium Cosapi-Dragados won the first contract to build the power station's main structures at a price of $23.461 million.
Brazil's Andrade Gutierrez SA was awarded the second contract to build the tunnel at San Gaban for $26.492 million.
Another Brazilian company, Constructora Norberto Odebrecht, won the third contract to build the machine-room for $24.603 million.
